# Torsion bar replacement and spring rates

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Select aftermarket torsion bars with a higher spring rate, adjust bar adjusters lower on the cross member due to increased stiffness, then consider shock compatibility. [t2251]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Select aftermarket torsion bars with a higher spring rate if you plan to carry heavy front accessories.
2. Adjust the bar adjusters so they sit lower on the cross member compared to stock due to increased stiffness.

_Procedure reported by [t2251]._

## Parts

- Aftermarket torsion bars: Options include 4X4 Parts, 30% higher rate or Calmini, 20% higher rate. [t2251]

## Tips & gotchas

- Consider the spring rate increase in relation to existing Bilstein shocks if not already accounted for. [t2251]
- Expect improved handling and reduced body roll once the vehicle is lifted. [t2251]
